source.quote: Greetings, travelers, and welcome back to Goldbound, the challenge series where our rogue Goldilocked is exploring the map of Azeroth one zone at a time. Each new zone can only be unlocked once he's earned a WOW token in his current zone. And currently, the price of a WoW token is hovering around 321,000 gold, and you only have 102,000 in the bags. And Goldilock has worked his way through Elwin. And now we're grinding through the nolles, rares, herbs, and fish of red. All for an elusive second token to unlock the next zone. And Goldilock's ultimate goal to explore all of Azeroth and earn the title of explorer. Now, this challenge isn't without its own restrictions, and Goldilock cannot buy items on the auction house or from other players. He can only sell on there, which means every copper, silver, and gold is coming from items collected within the zones. But that just makes the unlocks even sweeter. So, welcome back to Goldbound. Now, let's show Redidge Mountains what Goldie is really made of. All right, we're a little low on the gold tally. Of course, we could just sit around and wait for one of our many transmog pieces to sell, but there's no guarantee on when that's going to be. So, let's go ahead and set a challenge. A farm target will provide some fast selling materials and potentially some high ticket loot. We're talking about the fishing crates. Now, these have actually been a really fun way to switch up the farming here and there, and they can have a lot of hidden loot within them. So, how many should we farm? Well, we have about 70 bag slots available right now if we were to fill up our bags. But in a recent patch, the game bank was updated, and each tab is massive. Take a look. It's 7 by4, which accounts for a total of 98 bank slots.

All right, let's head back into Redidge for some more chances at loot. Up to this point, Goldilock has largely explored the Red Ridge loot tables, but not completely. source.quote: And if we look at the 6-month history of this item, it used to be sitting around 200k, but it's been climbing non-stop. And historical sales in the last 6 months have only ranged between 4 and 79,000. So really hard to justify the 700k price tag, but still it's on our target list. And what else is available in this area? Well, the Shadow Hide Darkw Weavers have a drop of their own, the Shadow Hide Scalper. And this item is listed on Wowhead as a 0.06% drop rate, even lower than the last one. But I'm not buying that. You see, this item was added in patch 1.11.1.1, Shadow of the Necropolis, way back in classic. But at this point in time, it actually dropped from the Shadow Height Assassins. The assassins are still around in these corners, but somewhere between patch 1 and patch 10, they took the scalper off the loot tables for the assassins and placed it on the dark weavers. And that's where Wowhead drop rates can get a little inaccurate because shadow high dark weavers have been in the game since patch 1.11.1, but the scalper was only added to the loot tables in patch 10 during dragon flight. So there's 10 expansions worth of loot data where it wasn't even possible to get. So the drop rate is artificially lower. And this actually seems to be the case for a lot of drops here in Redidge. But again, another one for the list because the market value is 63,000 gold. And with a region sale average over 6,000, I scrubbed through TSM data and found that eight of these have actually sold in the NA region in the last 6 months for between 6 and 15,000 gold. So, we have two decent targets from the Shadow Hide variants here. And intermingled between these two are Shadow Hide assassins, rabid Shadow Hide, Nolles, Shadow Hide Slayers, Brutes, and Warriors. Now, they're all worth taking down in a farm session for the Red Ridge world drop tables. We're talking bandit set, raider set, and soldier sets. And the Shadow Hide Warriors even have their own unique drop of the Shadow Hide Battle Axe. The region sale average on this one is only around 1k, but it does tend to move faster than the scalper and the mace, so definitely worth keeping posted if we can farm them. I will say it doesn't hurt that these mobs surround Row the silent. So far, we've gone dry on this rare with over 30 kills on Row for his big ticket items, but we should be able to snag a few more kills while we're in the area. Now, we'll see how many kills we can get on these shadow hide guys over the whole week and check back in with their progress near the end of the episode. Kill tracker engaged. But of course, with some more transmog on the table, it's time to return to a classic triedand-true method, dual gathering.

records.summary: One-hour full focus Elwynn/Redridge:295 Copper,30 Tin,37 Mageroyal,15 Swiftthistle,136 Silverleaf,63 Peacebloom,35 Briarthorn,111 Earthroot,26 Bruiseweed.2800 g raw appraisal, no shuffle.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/009 - I Opened 100 Redridge Fish Chests - Goldbound Episode 9.en-orig.txt
source.quote: And to be honest, this is a pretty stable method in these zones for some consistent gold income. As the series has developed, some of the Elwin shuff and redwood shuffle has become less profitable. But there's something to be said for the raw materials that sell consistently to move the needle towards the next zone. The plan this episode is to log some serious time on dual gathering to march forward. Because I'll be honest, I am getting anxious to get into that next zone. But for old times sake, let's go ahead and run a full power hour full focus just gathering mines and herbs to see what the potential raw gold per hour is. Now, this is not semi AFK Netflix watching farming. It's a full sprint. Let's see what kind of rates we can get. And as for the route, we're breaking out both the dual gathering, but also the dual zone loop, flying back and forth between our two unlocked zones, Elwin and Redidge. This gives us a wider spread of ores and herbs with plenty of time for nodes to respawn. And it keeps the loop fresh while the bags are filling. And if you look at this, right beside one of the nodes, a casualty dropped the traveler's backpack. An absolute best in slot bag for us at this stage, which means unfortunately our little fishing chest upgrade just slipped out of the rotation, but it is what it is and we got more bags now. Now, let's break down the hour sprint from a raw gold perspective. First off, we got 295 copper ore, which at about 4 gold, 18 silver each is a total of 1,233 gold. We also got 30 tin ore, which is only about 2 gold, 31 silver each for a total of 69. Nice. Moving on to the herbs, we got 37 mage royal totaling 118 gold, 15 swift thistle totaling 63 gold, 136 silver leaf totaling 459 gold, 63 peace bloom totaling 259 gold, 35 brierthorn totaling 128 gold, 111 earthroot totaling 397 gold, and 26 bruiseed about 75 gold total. Now, this is a wide spread of different herbs and ores. But if you total it all up, even without a shuffle, that's 2,800 raw gold in a single hour. Not bad at all. And we've stacked a fair amount of raw mats. But unless some transmog starts moving soon, it looks like we're going to need to log some serious hours on some of these consistent farms. And on that note, let me level with you travelers. The sales out of Redidge on Transmog really aren't popping the way we hoped. I mean, don't get me wrong, we've been getting the drops, and in fact, we have over 400 auctions posted with an item value north of a million gold, but we all know the truth. Transmog is the long game, and some of these just might not move for months or even years. But of course, we don't want to be stuck in Red Ridge for years. We want into the next zone and that means we do need to lean into some of these steady farms. The dual gathering loops, the Condor eggs, and a few other staples that just consistently stack the bags. With only a handful of unique farms left to explore in Redidge, you can expect us to start revisiting some of our best hitters from back in Elwin as well. And I'm afraid you might already know which one I'm talking about. Now, on the transmog front, it feels like the wind has dropped out of the sails a little bit. But rest assured, the Goldbound grind is only speeding up from here because thanks to your support on these videos, the streams, and from our sponsors, we're making the leap to full-time content creation. And that means more streams, more content, faster unlocks, and more adventures for all of us travelers. So, thank you. And if you want to catch the grind live, you can find me over at twitch.tv/pathalericsold.

source.quote: Right now, we're going to do it Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Fridays starting at 10:00 a.m. Mountain time. Now, don't worry. The YouTube series will always be the true heart of Goldbound, but the streams are a chance to hang out, share the grind, and push this challenge forward together. And speaking of which, we've got some gold to make. So, let's hit the gas and get back at it. And while we're talking Red Ridge, there are a few vendor tricks that are absolutely worth scooping up and posting on the auction house. Let me show you. Now, first up, right here in Lake Shaw itself, among the tradesmen, you'll find Doran Songblade. And wouldn't you know it, the man sells the very gear he's wearing, the scale mail set. And on the auction house, these pieces float around 200 to 300 gold each. And even though Doran will hand them over for a few copper, I'll admit it. Even I didn't know he was here for a while. So, the odds are plenty of other players don't either, and might pick these up on the auction house. And next door is his shield crafting colleague Cara Adams. Now she only has two items, both shields. First off, the ring to buckler, which fetches around 800 gold from a 74 copper sale. But the real ticket here is the large metal shield with a market value that shows as high as 6.4K. But let's be real, the actual average sales of these two shields are probably closer in the hundreds, not the thousands. But when you're buying for under a silver, any sale is pretty much pure profit. And of course, there's also Amy Davenport, the local trade goods vendor. Now, at first glance, her wares look ordinary until you flip over to the recipe tab. There, tucked away is the pattern of the black welp tunic worth around 1,000 gold in the auction house.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/009 - I Opened 100 Redridge Fish Chests - Goldbound Episode 9.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Right now, we're going to do it Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Fridays starting at 10:00 a.m. Mountain time. Now, don't worry. The YouTube series will always be the true heart of Goldbound, but the streams are a chance to hang out, share the grind, and push this challenge forward together. And speaking of which, we've got some gold to make. So, let's hit the gas and get back at it. And while we're talking Red Ridge, there are a few vendor tricks that are absolutely worth scooping up and posting on the auction house. Let me show you. Now, first up, right here in Lake Shaw itself, among the tradesmen, you'll find Doran Songblade. And wouldn't you know it, the man sells the very gear he's wearing, the scale mail set. And on the auction house, these pieces float around 200 to 300 gold each. And even though Doran will hand them over for a few copper, I'll admit it. Even I didn't know he was here for a while. So, the odds are plenty of other players don't either, and might pick these up on the auction house. And next door is his shield crafting colleague Cara Adams. Now she only has two items, both shields. First off, the ring to buckler, which fetches around 800 gold from a 74 copper sale. But the real ticket here is the large metal shield with a market value that shows as high as 6.4K. But let's be real, the actual average sales of these two shields are probably closer in the hundreds, not the thousands. But when you're buying for under a silver, any sale is pretty much pure profit. And of course, there's also Amy Davenport, the local trade goods vendor. Now, at first glance, her wares look ordinary until you flip over to the recipe tab. There, tucked away is the pattern of the black welp tunic worth around 1,000 gold in the auction house.

source.quote: And we are starting to see frayed knots make their way through. I've got a feeling we'll be seeing a few more of those before the clear is over. And scrolling down, we do have a healthy amount of transmog sales in the 200 to 400 gold range. Individually, they're kind of small, but together they do start stacking up into something a little more substantive. Among the highlights, another scimitar of a tune. And actually, we sold a couple of those this week alongside a null Punisher. It seems like the Red Ridge weapons are carrying the mid-range ticket sales right now. And here's a fun one. Remember that black welp tunic? Well, we actually sold one already. Not a bad flip for how much copper it cost us. And let's go ahead and get this mailbox fully opened and enjoy the classic cha-ching of the gold rolling in.

source.quote: And the final tally for the week is 35,136 gold, which is respectable given the rates in the zone. But like I said, it's time we hit that gas pedal. And for those tracking the grind with me, our slash played is now at 9 days 17 hours with a grand total of 135,000 gold in the bags. Plenty of farming ahead and plenty of trade goods to keep moving. Let's get back out there and keep it rolling. Go with honor, friend.
